Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the driver's decision to enter the field, as the community grapples with the sudden loss and the trauma inflicted upon the young athletes and their families. why_it_matters_bullets: This incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in public recreational safety and underscores the urgent need for enhanced physical barriers around youth sports facilities to prevent vehicular incursions. sources.headline: Pope Leo Looks Ahead After Cancer Surgery
sources.content: NPR All Things Considered co-host and American Pope coauthor Scott Detrow tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Pope Leo XIV’s cancer was detected early and that his recovery appears to be progressing as he prepares to resume his duties and travel to South America. sources.headline: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
sources.content: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.(Image credit: Alessandra Tarantino)

brief_bullets: Pope Leo has made his first public appearance in St. Peter’s Square following a successful lung cancer surgery, signaling a significant milestone in his recovery. The pontiff, who was discharged from the hospital just four days after the procedure, addressed the faithful to confirm his intention to gradually resume his full slate of ecclesiastical and administrative duties. This rapid transition from clinical care to public engagement underscores both the success of the medical intervention and the Pope's commitment to maintaining continuity within the Vatican’s leadership. By appearing before the public so soon after his operation, the Pope aims to reassure the global Catholic community regarding his health and his capacity to continue guiding the Church. His return marks a pivotal moment for the Holy See, as the administration prepares to transition back to normal operations following a brief period of uncertainty regarding the pontiff's physical well-being.
why_it_matters_bullets: The Pope's swift return to public life stabilizes the Vatican's internal governance and mitigates potential speculation regarding his long-term ability to lead the Church. This recovery trajectory ensures that the Holy See remains focused on its strategic global agenda without the disruption of a prolonged leadership vacuum.

Akhlaqi, recognized for his extensive background in defense technology, assumes this pivotal role at a moment of extreme geopolitical volatility. His confirmation signals the Iranian government's intent to prioritize technical expertise and rapid military modernization as the country navigates the escalating pressures of a multi-front war. By filling this vacancy with a specialist in defense systems, Tehran aims to stabilize its command structure and maintain operational continuity amidst the intensifying regional hostilities that have already claimed significant members of its military hierarchy.

sources.headline: Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by police
sources.content: Mumbai: Twenty-two IIT Bombay students, including eight who were allegedly detained twice in a single day, were picked up by the police from inside the campus on Sunday amid their ongoing protest demanding justice for deceased Sahil Wakode, student bodies said.The protesters and student collectives alleged that police used extreme force during the crackdown, accusing the cops of tearing their clothes, kicking and choking them. All detained students were taken to the Powai police station, they said.Police and IIT B authorities are yet to issue a detailed official statement regarding the scale of the detentions and the allegations of excessive force.Students have been protesting near the campus gates in the Powai area for a month, including a 15-day hunger strike, raising allegations of caste discrimination and institutional apathy surrounding the death of 22-year-old Sahil Wakode.IIT Bombay suicide: Sahil Wakode apologised for cheating in exam, sought second chance, say policeThe second-year B.Tech student was found dead in his hostel room on September 18 after allegedly being caught cheating during a mid-semester exam. Sunday marked one month since his alleged suicide, prompting students to plan a memorial and a ‘mashal juloos’ (torchlight procession).Student representatives alleged that police barged into the campus in large numbers in the morning. After an initial detention and brief release, students gathered at the protest site, alongside Wakode’s grieving parents to pay tribute, they said.Protesters alleged that the campus security and police subsequently dismantled the protest site and forcibly removed the participants. They also claimed that female students faced inappropriate touching and physical assault. A total of 22 students were detained, they said.The demonstrators also targeted the IIT Bombay administration over the deployment of police inside the campus, asking who authorised it.Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad and representatives of several Ambedkarite organisations subsequently reached the spot and staged a demonstration demanding an immediate meeting with the Chairperson of the Board of Governors and the Director.While officials from the Powai police station were not immediately available for comment, the institute authorities were yet to share their response to the detentions and allegations of excessive force.Wakode’s parents have been continuing their hunger strike at Azan Maidan in south Mumbai, demanding action and accountability from the institute administration.They have accused Professor Suryanarayana Doolla of harassment and caste-based discrimination. Earlier this month, the police questioned Doolla for nearly 10 hours in connection with the alleged suicide.

sources.headline: '56-inch ka seena kahan hai': Rahul Gandhi slams Modi-Shah, CEC over 'vote chori'
sources.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of orchestrating alleged “vote theft” behind the scenes, claiming that Union Home Minister Amit Shah operationalised it and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar implemented it.Addressing a rally in Margao in South Goa on the concluding day of the Congress's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', Gandhi alleged that Modi, Shah and Kumar were facing mounting pressure over the party's allegations of electoral malpractice.“There is no confusion anymore. Gyanesh Kumar implements the vote theft, Amit Shah operationalises it, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi does the entire planning from behind the scenes,” Gandhi said.The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha warned that the three would face justice over the alleged irregularities. He also claimed that the Congress had evidence of electoral malpractice in several states, including Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam.“PM Modi, Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar will face justice and pay the price for what they have done,” he said.Gandhi had led protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and Kumar in New Delhi. He alleged that opposition votes had been deleted, votes added in favour of the ruling party, and voters shifted between districts or brought in from other states.Claiming that more than 45 defamation cases had been filed against him, including by people associated with Modi and Shah, Gandhi said no case had been filed over his allegations of vote theft. He suggested that the government was reluctant to pursue the matter legally because it could lead to a full-fledged legal battle.Urging voters to give the Congress a full majority in the 2027 Goa Assembly elections, Gandhi called on party workers to continue engaging with people across the state.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'“You think about Goa. In Delhi, in a short while, we will deal with Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. You don't need to worry about that. The work is underway; their expiry date is approaching,” he said.Gandhi also accused the BJP-led Union government of favouring industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani by awarding them infrastructure projects, land and other economic opportunities in exchange for political support and publicity.“This is their system. This is how their system works: give billionaires money, give them contracts, give them land. In return, the billionaires do their marketing,” he alleged.Turning to Goa, Gandhi accused the state government of taking land from farmers and economically weaker sections and transferring it to outsiders and associates. He alleged that the cancellation of the regional master plan had enabled the government to facilitate such transfers, putting the state's natural resources and cultural heritage at risk.“Goa is a paradise, one of the most beautiful places in the country, with a great culture,” he said, alleging that its land was being handed over to billionaires.The Congress leader further claimed that Goa had the country's highest unemployment rate, forcing young people to seek opportunities abroad. He accused the BJP government of dismantling the state's employment structure and described its functioning as a “special Goa model of corruption”, drawing a comparison with the Gujarat model associated with Modi.On education, Gandhi criticised the alleged use of force against student protesters in Delhi and accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of influencing university appointments. He said students were raising concerns over electoral malpractice, unemployment, education costs and inflation.“This country does not belong to any one organisation. This country does not belong to the RSS. This country does not belong to the BJP. This country belongs to the people of India,” he said.Gandhi added that Goa belonged to its people, not its chief minister or ministers, and called for access to education, healthcare and employment, alongside environmental protection.Taking a swipe at the Prime Minister, Gandhi questioned the absence of Modi's often-cited “56-inch seena”, saying he could not stand in front of his political opponents.He urged Congress workers to continue the party's fight against the BJP's ideology beyond the conclusion of the yatra.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Goa Congress leaders Yuri Alemao and Girish Chodankar, began on September 22 and covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in the coastal state. The party said the campaign aimed to protect Goa's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity while strengthening its grassroots presence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.(With PTI Inputs)

brief_bullets: Senator Marco Rubio has indicated that President-elect Donald Trump intends to utilize a window of up to 60 days to carefully evaluate the implementation of potential sanctions against Russia. This strategic pause suggests a deliberate approach by the incoming administration to assess the geopolitical landscape and the specific impact of trade-related measures, including tariff relief considerations for nations like India. By signaling this timeline, the Trump transition team is signaling a departure from immediate, reactive policy shifts in favor of a more calculated review process that balances domestic economic interests with complex international diplomatic relations. This period of deliberation will likely serve as a critical phase for the administration to refine its broader foreign policy framework, particularly regarding the ongoing conflict in Ukraine and the intricate web of global energy and trade dependencies that define current U.S.-Russia interactions.
why_it_matters_bullets: This 60-day review period signals a methodical approach to foreign policy that prioritizes leverage and negotiation over immediate escalation, potentially reshaping global trade alliances and the efficacy of future sanctions regimes.

sources.headline: India bars sugarcane-based ethanol from 2026-27 procurement tender to safeguard sugar supplies
sources.content: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies have excluded ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from their latest procurement tender for the 2026-27 supply year, following government directions to halt sugar diversion for fuel amid concerns over domestic availability and prices.Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), acting on behalf of the oil marketing companies, issued the tender on October 16 seeking bids for approximately 11 billion litres of ethanol. The volume is intended to support the nationwide target of blending 20 per cent ethanol in petrol during the supply year that runs from November 2026 to October 2027.The tender document states: “The Government of India has issued directions that sugar diversion for ethanol be reduced to zero for ethanol supply year 2026-27.” It adds that “no offers have been sought for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses.”Instead, the companies will accept bids for ethanol made from maize, broken rice, surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India, and C-heavy molasses. The procurement price for maize-based ethanol has also been reduced to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86, cutting the incentive from Rs 5.79 to Rs 2.79 per litre.Sugar, ethanol and the policy balance: Why India needs predictable rules over crisis controlsThe restrictions come after poor rainfall in major sugar-producing states such as Maharashtra and Karnataka raised the prospect of lower output. India, the world’s largest sugar consumer, has faced rising domestic prices and concerns that continued diversion of cane and sugar into ethanol could tighten food supplies.The ethanol-blended petrol programme has relied on both sugarcane- and grain-based feedstock to cut crude oil imports and reduce vehicle emissions. India has rolled out E20 fuel — petrol containing up to 20 per cent ethanol — as the national standard. Officials view the latest tender as an effort to maintain the blending targets while prioritising sugar availability for consumption and containing prices.

brief_bullets: Kolkata police have arrested seven individuals, including key organizers of the Chorbagan Durga Puja, following a catastrophic stampede that resulted in 19 fatalities and 25 injuries. The tragedy, which has sparked intense political finger-pointing between the All India Trinamool Congress and state leadership, was reportedly exacerbated by severe mismanagement, confusing crowd control announcements, and dangerously narrow entry points. Simultaneously, the Indian government has taken a significant policy shift by barring sugarcane-based ethanol from the 2026-27 procurement tender to prioritize domestic sugar supplies and stabilize market prices. These developments highlight a dual crisis of public safety accountability and resource management, as authorities face mounting pressure to address systemic failures in both event crowd control and national agricultural-energy policy. The intersection of these events underscores the ongoing challenges in maintaining public order during massive cultural gatherings and the complexities of balancing industrial fuel demands against essential food security.
why_it_matters_bullets: The arrests signal a hardening stance on public safety accountability, while the ethanol policy shift reflects a strategic pivot toward prioritizing food security over renewable energy targets to mitigate inflationary pressures.

sources.headline: Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt as suspected Lawrence Bishnoi gang members open fire
sources.content: Mumbai: Bollywood’s action star Tiger Shroff came under a chilling real-life threat on Sunday evening when three unidentified motorcycle-borne men allegedly opened fire at him near Pushpa Park in Mumbai’s upscale Juhu area.Shroff  escaped unhurt in the firing, sending a shock through the film fraternity as senior police officers rushed to the spot to investigate the incident off the Pushpa Park area of Juhu. Tiger Shroff's driver who sustained a gun shot wound on his left hand, is out of danger.Another person is reported to be injured, however, details are awaited.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has claimed responsibility for the incident and has asked the actor to apologise to the underworld don. Doctor gets extortion call from man claiming to be Lawrence Bishnoi gang member; 1 held in DelhiA purported audio clip also went viral on social media platforms in which one person named Anil Pandit claimed that anyone working with Salman Khan will not be spared. Shroff (36) is the son of the legendary actor Jackie Shroff and Ayesha Dutt. Tiger Shroff, a martial arts experts and fitness enthusiast,  made his Bollywood debut with Heropanti and went on to headline popular franchises such as Baaghi and War, establishing himself as one of Hindi cinema’s prominent action stars.The incident took place around 7.30 pm when he was headed home after a football match. The Juhu Police station and Crime Branch-CID of Mumbai Police have launched massive investigations to track down the suspects. The police has formed 15 teams to track down the  culprit.Forensic experts too are collecting evidence from the site.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who is also the state Home Minister, was briefed by top officials including Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti  about the incident.Salman Khan, Rohit Shetty targets of  Bishnoi gang In the recent past, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang had targeted actor Salman Khan and filmmaker Rohit Shetty. Over the last few years, the Bishnoi gang repeatedly targeted Salman Khan and even opened fire towards his Galaxy Apartments home on Bandra Seaface. The rivalry stems from the 1998 blackbuck poaching case, in which actor Salman Khan was accused of killing a blackbuck—an animal sacred to the Bishnoi community. On 1 February, 2026, in the wee hours, a group of persons linked to the Bishnoi gang aimed their pistol fire towards the home of Rohit Shetty’s nine-storey home in Juhu - and one of the bullets hit the glass of the gym inside the building. Bishnoi gang eliminated Baba Siddique It may be recalled that former Maharashtra minister and NCP leader Baba Siddique—who was considered close to the Hindi entertainment industry—was shot dead by members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang on 12 October 2024 in the Bandra East area of Mumbai. As many as 27 arrested people have been charge-sheeted in the case.

brief_bullets: Across the United States, the 'No Kings' movement has mobilized supporters through a series of coordinated rallies designed to emphasize the importance of early voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. These demonstrations serve as a public platform for activists to advocate for democratic accountability and voter participation, specifically targeting the perceived concentration of executive power. By encouraging citizens to cast their ballots before Election Day, organizers aim to mitigate potential logistical bottlenecks and ensure that voter turnout remains robust throughout the early voting window. The rallies reflect a broader national discourse regarding the health of American institutions and the necessity of civic engagement in shaping legislative outcomes. As these events gain momentum, they highlight a growing grassroots effort to influence the political landscape by prioritizing proactive electoral participation over traditional last-minute voting patterns.
why_it_matters_bullets: The 'No Kings' campaign underscores a strategic shift toward early mobilization as a tool to secure electoral outcomes and counter political apathy. This trend signals that grassroots organizations are increasingly prioritizing long-term institutional influence over reactive campaign cycles, potentially altering the traditional timeline of American electioneering.

brief_bullets: A devastating tragedy unfolded in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, when a speeding truck breached police barricades and plowed into a crowd of pilgrims gathered near the Sheetlamata Mandir, resulting in at least 15 fatalities and dozens of injuries. The incident occurred around 1:30 am as the vehicle, bearing Punjab registration plates, reportedly suffered a brake failure, causing the driver to lose control before crashing into the temple’s outer wall and gate. While investigators suggest the driver swerved to avoid a larger crowd of hundreds, the vehicle’s unauthorized entry into a restricted zone has sparked intense scrutiny regarding local security protocols and traffic enforcement. In response to the catastrophe, Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his condolences and announced financial ex gratia relief for the victims and their families. Local authorities have launched an extensive search for the driver, who fled the scene immediately following the collision, as rescue operations continue under the supervision of senior officials.

sources.headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran’s legal challenge to leave India notice
Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row
sources.content: Mumbai: Actor-filmmaker Aamir Khan met Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray at his residence in Mumbai on Sunday.The details of the meeting were not immediately known.The meeting comes days after Aamir Khan's nephew and actor Imran Khan was served a notice by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. Imran had reportedly participated in the October 10 protests at August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.The 43-year-old Imran Khan is a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeHe has challenged the notice in the Bombay High Court, which is expected to hear the matter this week. The plea is expected to be mentioned for an urgent hearing before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.“The notice has been issued without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention. It was issued without inquiry, a show-cause notice, or any opportunity for the Petitioner (Khan) to respond to the alleged violations,” the plea stated.The FRRO issued the notice under Sections 7 and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, directing Imran Khan to leave India by October 28, 2026.

stories.primary_headline: Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA

primary_source.headline: Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
primary_source.content: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital. These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer.&nbsp;The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated.&nbsp;Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier. This order is expected to reduce the MRP of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by 70 per cent, depending on their current price structures.&nbsp;The 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy drugs used for treating over 20 types of cancers, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim, which is used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients and bevacizumab, which is the approved drug to treat colon, ovarian, and cervical cancer. With this notification, MRP of widely used anti-cancer drugs such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib is expected to become more accessible for cancer patients.Anti-cancer drug prices to come down as govt caps trade margins at 30%Centre caps trade margins on cancer medicines at 30% of MRPMarket overview: scheduled vs non-scheduled drugsCurrently, the anti-cancer drugs market comprises nearly 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs 12,500 crore. Of this, scheduled cancer drugs that come under price control account for approximately Rs 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs.To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels. NPPA has clearly stated: "The manufacturers of the formulations are required to maintain the present production levels. Any manufacturer intending to lower the average monthly production levels will seek prior permission from NPPA. Further, any manufacturer intending to discontinue production of the above-said formulations shall furnish information to NPPA."&nbsp;How is the new price calculated?The manufacturers of non–scheduled formulations, selling branded or generic or both the versions of formulations at MRP higher than the MRP should revise their prices using this formula:&nbsp; MRP of the product = Price to Stockist or Price to Distributor x {1 + (Trade Margin/(100 − Trade Margin))} + Applicable GST.&nbsp;Citing an example, NPPA explained: For a non-scheduled anti-cancer formulation with current MRP: Rs 300 + Applicable GST. However, the price to a distributor is Rs 70. Maximum allowable revised MRP as per formula shall be: Rs70x{1+(30/(100−30))} = Rs 100 + Applicable GST.&nbsp;The notification has also clarified: "All the existing manufacturers of formulations having MRP lower than the MRP so computed … shall maintain their existing MRP."

stories.primary_headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body

primary_source.headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: As the Election Commission "resumes" distribution of "readable" electoral rolls to parties after a "gap of eight years", Congress on Sunday said "nothing can save" Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar while insisting that a "thorough" revamp of the poll body and its IT system is required.General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh said the decision to provide electoral rolls in readable PDF format  was the result of the whole nation being on the streets against the "vote chors".EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23The attack comes as the Congress prepares to host I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties at a rally in Ramlila Maidan on November 1 against the CEC.In a post on 'X', he said over the past two years, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have been "persistent, insistent and consistent" in demanding that the EC provide electoral rolls in searchable format to all parties. पिछले दो वर्षों से लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता श्री राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस पार्टी लगातार, मजबूती से और पुरजोर तरीके से यह मांग करते आ रहे हैं कि भारत निर्वाचन आयोग सभी राजनीतिक दलों को मतदाता सूची ऐसे डिजिटल फॉर्मेट में उपलब्ध कराए, जिसमें मतदाताओं के नाम और अन्य जानकारी आसानी से…&mdash; Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 18, 2026
 

"The demand was repeatedly refused by the ECI - which stopped providing searchable voter rolls in 2018 when the Congress found lakhs of bogus voters in Madhya Pradesh. The demand was denied for eight years to enable 'vote chori'," he claimed.Referring to the October 15 announcement by the EC on providing voter lists in readable format, he said "every time Vote Chori is caught, the Modi government adopts a new tactic: stopping readable voter rolls, fake voter additions, SIR. But not this time.""Nothing can save the CEC Gyanesh Kumar who, acting on the instructions of the PM and the HM, has destroyed public trust and confidence in the ECI. He simply has to go. But that alone will not be enough. The ECI itself along with its IT system has to be thoroughly revamped," he said. TThe SIR, that has put the Constitutional right to vote for over 13 crore Indians at risk, has to be suspended forthwith, he added.

sources.headline: EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23
sources.content: New Delhi: The 'People Against SIR', a coalition of various organisations, on Sunday announced a ‘People’s March to Reclaim Democracy’ on October 23 across India demanding removal and prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and restoration of voters whose names have been deleted.With the slogan ‘Har Haath Mein Tiranga, Har Gali Jantar Mantar’ (In Every Hand Tricolor, Every Street is Jantar Mantar), the coalition of civil society organisations, farmer unions, trade unions, students and youth organisations, academicians, artistes and activists said the protest marches with tricolor in their hands will be held at tehsil, district, state and national level.Nothing can save CEC; SIR must be suspended forthwith: CongressThe coalition, which included actor-activist Prakash Raj, Kisan Sabha leader P Krishnaprasad and CPI(ML)L leader N Sai Balaji, said the ‘People's March’ will not request police permission anywhere while "strictly warning" police, paramilitary and prisons against using the "brute state force" against peaceful protesters.&nbsp;If the march is blocked by police, it said, the protesters will peacefully hold the People's Parliament and disperse later after singing the national anthem.Claiming that the CEC helped the BJP to remain in power, it recalled that the Supreme Court has maintained that it did not upheld alteration of Form 6 used for inclusion of new voters.&nbsp;“Gyanesh Kumar has violated his Constitutional pledge and must be prosecuted. But the Prime Minister himself is protecting the criminal...Without Parliament impeaching CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the Prime Minister cannot come out of the full-blown constitutional standoff,” it said.Calling upon farmers, workers, daily wage earners, traders, entrepreneurs, journalists, advocates, teachers, employees, artists, intellectuals, women, youth, students, adivasis, dalits and minorities to join the march, a statement said its demands include comprehensive electoral reforms, proportional representation, curb money/muscle power and legalise state funding of polls.The statement alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have misused the Election Commission and erased the voting rights of 13.41 crore citizens through SIR.

sources.headline: Chacarra earns third win of year to move top of Race to Dubai standings
sources.content: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots with the Spaniard's third victory of the season moving him top of the Race to Dubai standings, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy, with three events remaining.

brief_bullets: Spanish golfer Eugenio Chacarra has ascended to the top of the Race to Dubai standings following a decisive two-shot victory at the DP World India Championship. This triumph marks his third win of the season, a significant achievement that propels him past high-profile competitors including Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy in the season-long rankings. With only three events remaining on the calendar, Chacarra has explicitly identified securing a spot on the Ryder Cup team as his primary objective, signaling a shift in his competitive trajectory. His consistent performance throughout the tournament underscores his rising influence in professional golf, as he leverages this momentum to challenge established stars for the tour's ultimate honors. The victory not only validates his current form but also places him in a commanding position to dictate the narrative for the remainder of the season as he pursues both the Race to Dubai title and international team selection. Chacarra’s ascent disrupts the traditional hierarchy of the Race to Dubai, forcing established stars to recalibrate their strategies as the season reaches its climax. His success highlights a shifting competitive landscape that could fundamentally alter the composition and selection dynamics for the upcoming Ryder Cup.

brief_bullets: The Indian box office is witnessing a significant surge in activity as Yami Gautam’s latest cinematic venture, Nayyi Navelli, successfully crossed the Rs 10 crore mark within just two days of its theatrical release. This strong performance highlights the growing audience appetite for mid-budget, star-driven dramas that resonate with contemporary viewers. Simultaneously, the industry is closely monitoring the historic run of Rajinikanth’s blockbuster Jailer 2, which is rapidly approaching the prestigious Rs 400 crore milestone by its third day. Director Nelson Dilipkumar has further fueled public excitement by sharing behind-the-scenes imagery with the legendary actor, underscoring the film's massive cultural footprint. These concurrent successes demonstrate a robust recovery and sustained momentum for the domestic film market, as both established superstars and compelling new narratives continue to draw large crowds back to cinema halls across the country. The simultaneous success of these films signals a healthy, diversified box office ecosystem capable of sustaining multiple high-performing projects, which bolsters investor confidence and encourages continued investment in both regional and national cinema.

brief_bullets: A catastrophic fire at CFB Wainwright, one of Canada’s most prominent military training installations in Alberta, has resulted in multiple fatalities and several injuries, prompting an urgent emergency response. Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed the tragedy, characterizing the situation as an active and delicate operation while noting that severe, high-velocity winds significantly hampered containment efforts and exacerbated the blaze. Local medical facilities have been mobilized to treat the wounded, with attending physicians describing the scale of the emergency as a disaster. As authorities continue to monitor the site, the incident has triggered a comprehensive investigation into the origins of the fire and the adequacy of safety protocols at the base. This event marks a significant blow to the Canadian Armed Forces, raising immediate questions regarding infrastructure security and the operational readiness of critical training facilities during periods of extreme environmental volatility.
why_it_matters_bullets: The incident at CFB Wainwright threatens to disrupt essential military training cycles and necessitates a rigorous review of safety standards at high-security government installations. Beyond the immediate human toll, the loss of life and infrastructure could force a strategic reassessment of emergency preparedness and fire mitigation protocols across Canada’s defense network.

stories.primary_headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target

primary_source.headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target
primary_source.content: Kolkata: The stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has triggered a war of words in West Bengal politics, as the alleged association of two ruling Bharatiya Janata Party leaders and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s nephew with the organisers provided fresh ammunition to the Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress to attack the government.Suvendu, himself, on October 12, inaugurated the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity’s pandal, where a stampede left 19 people dead and more than 20 injured on Sunday. The narrow entry and exit alleyways, limited space and inadequate crowd-control measures, deliberately dim lighting to match the pandal's theme, a sudden influx of visitors seeking shelter from the evening rain, and alleged lapses in police arrangements are blamed for the disaster.With Suvendu’s nephew, Debdeep Adhikari, being the chief patron of the organising committee, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, the TMC faction led by Mamata Banerjee, finally found a ‘bhaipo’ in the ruling BJP to train the guns on.&nbsp;“Guess who is closely associated with the Chorebagan Puja Pandal? CM Suvendu Adhikari’s BHAIPO,” the MAITC posted on X soon after the disaster. “When are you going to put your criminal nephew behind bars, Suvendu Babu?” posted Abhishek Banerjee, who has been at the receiving end of the ‘bhaipo (nephew)’ taunt ever since his ‘pisi (aunt)’, Mamata Banerjee, inducted him into the party she founded.The tragedy raised questions about whether the organisers had made adequate safety arrangements for the large crowds expected at the pandal. Its narrow entry and exit passageways, sloping route through the structure, and deliberately dim lighting intended to complement its theme may have heightened the risk of overcrowding and slowed visitor movement. The sudden influx of people seeking shelter from the evening rain further compounded the danger, while questions were raised about the police's preparedness to regulate the crowds and respond to the emergency.Not only Debdeep, but two other BJP leaders were also associated with this year’s Durga Puja of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsav Samity, legislator Vijay Ojha as chairman and the saffron party’s North Kolkata district unit president, Tamoghna Ghosh, as chief adviser.The six people arrested by police after the incident include the secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and the vice president of the organising committee Santanu Dubey, but none are linked to the BJP.“The CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan Puja Pandal. Did he not look into security arrangements when he visited the pandal? Won’t he be held accountable for every single life lost?” the Mamata faction of the TMC asked, questioning whether the police would take any action against Debdeep, Vijay and Tamoghna.Soon after the stampede on Saturday, Suvendu and Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, where the injured and deceased were initially taken. The chief minister visited the stampede site in the pre-dawn hours of Sunday.“Attempts are being made by some people to reap political dividends from such a tragedy. They will not succeed. The families of the deceased and injured told me that they had full faith in the state government and me,” Suvendu said on Sunday. He added that a probe was underway and the government would not spare anyone found responsible for the disaster. “No one should indulge in politics over death,” he said.&nbsp;Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govtHe sought to turn the tables on his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, and the TMC government she had headed.&nbsp;The chief minister cited several tragedies during the TMC’s tenure, including the collapse of an under-construction flyover in north Kolkata in 2016, which killed seven people, and the collapse of Majherhat Bridge in 2018, which killed three. He also referred to the Panihati festival incident in July 2022, in which three people died; the electrocution deaths of nine people during waterlogging in Kolkata after heavy rain ahead of Durga Puja in 2025; and flash floods in North Bengal that year, which killed around 100 people.“What was the then chief minister doing?” Suvendu questioned, hitting back at Mamata.&nbsp;“This is not the time to indulge in a political blame game,” Samik Bhattacharya, the state BJP chief, said, responding to the Opposition's criticism. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Opposition, however, is not ready to relent. “Where were the police when the incident took place? There was no response even after calls were made to the police control room,” Subhankar Sarkar, president of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, said.What further sharpened criticism of the city police and the state government is that, over the past few days, cops in several places were seen evicting or trying to evict bookstalls set up by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) near the Durga Puja pandals. Mohammed Salim, the state secretary of the CPI(M), questioned the priorities of the police, stating that the residents living near the pandal of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Samity complained about a lack of police to manage the crowd as well as the unavailability of an adequate number of ambulances to take the injured to hospital after the disaster.&nbsp;As in several other Durga Puja organising clubs across West Bengal, the leadership of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity changed after the TMC’s defeat in the Assembly elections earlier this year and the BJP’s rise to power. Jayanta Bandopadhyay, who was known to be associated with the TMC, was removed from the puja committee’s leadership, although he had managed the festival for several years. Jayanta had also performed the Khunti Puja, the ceremony marking the start of pandal construction, before he and others were sidelined and a new committee comprising people linked to the ruling BJP was formed. The new committee subsequently performed a second Khunti Puja in the presence of several BJP leaders.

Jayanta had also performed the Khunti Puja, the ceremony marking the start of pandal construction, before he and others were sidelined and a new committee comprising people linked to the ruling BJP was formed. The new committee subsequently performed a second Khunti Puja in the presence of several BJP leaders.

primary_source.headline: Attacked from the sky: Sudanese goldminers count deadly cost of eking out a living on the Egypt border
primary_source.content: As civil war has left their country in ruins, many young Sudanese have turned to artisanal mining. stories.primary_headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg

primary_source.headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
primary_source.content: The St Petersburg Oil Terminal was among targets hit in the city overnight The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five. A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit. Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week. Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing. It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

stories.primary_headline: France wakes up to one of its worst bouts of unrest in years; one dead, 500 cops injured

primary_source.headline: France wakes up to one of its worst bouts of unrest in years; one dead, 500 cops injured
primary_source.content:
Paris: France woke on Sunday to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested.Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris, where police made a record 855 arrests. Across France, police detained some 1,800 people and more than 500 officers were injured, the interior minister said.More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services.While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers."No room for violence in our Republic," President Emmanuel Macron posted on X as the unrest unfolded late on Saturday. "Those who have ransacked, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished."Aucune place pour la violence dans notre République.Ceux qui ont cassé, attaqué les préfectures comme les commerces, pillé jusqu’à nos mairies, seront poursuivis et punis.Aux forces de l’ordre, garantes du droit à manifester, je dis le soutien de la Nation.Nous ferons tous…&mdash; Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) October 17, 2026
 

A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.Unrest mars day of violent protest in France, as student movement turns nationalIn Paris, smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and spray-painted slogans bore witness to a day that began largely with peaceful demonstrations but descended into violence.In Limoges, workers assessed the damage to the 143-year-old city hall, which was partially destroyed in an arson attack.The unrest has increased pressure on Macron and his government. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals, with a presidential election due next year.Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.

stories.primary_headline: Rep. Veasey Calls for Scrutiny of Trump Russia Ties

primary_source.headline: Rep. Veasey Calls for Scrutiny of Trump Russia Ties
primary_source.content: Rep. Marc Veasey, a Texas Democrat, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s recent moves involving Russia and Ukraine warrant greater congressional scrutiny, while warning that questions over Ukraine’s access to US military technology could undermine allies’ confidence in American defense products. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Veasey also says Tarrant County will be crucial to Democrats’ chances in Texas, arguing that strong performance there could help Senate candidate James Talarico win statewide. (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.primary_headline: NHS data breaches a disgrace, says health secretary

primary_source.headline: NHS data breaches a disgrace, says health secretary
primary_source.content: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were killed in the Nottingham attacks Speaking to the BBC, Yvette Cooper said she expected action to be taken against staff who have breached NHS data and privacy standards. Dr Manjeet Shehmar, NUH medical director, previously said there was "simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason". Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper said "there's got to be proper respect for patients" from NHS staff. "Let me be really clear about this," she said. "There are proper data and privacy standards across the NHS. Students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.

primary_source.headline: The playground murder - trauma, loss and a love that endured
primary_source.content: Best friends Diane (left) and Pauline (right) did everything together Pauline watched as 16-year-old Diane collapsed after the knife attack by another pupil and then helped to carry her across the road to the arms of her parents who lived in an upstairs flat within view of the school. Diane's murder would not only devastate her family, her friends and the local community, its shockwaves would go on to be felt for decades. Diane Watson was 16 when she died Thirty-five years later, Pauline Love Thomson has spoken for the first time about the trauma of that April morning when she was just 16. Pauline describes how a large crowd of schoolkids gathered round as Glover shouted at Diane while waving the knife - and the chilling moment she dealt the deadly blow.

stories.primary_headline: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail

primary_source.headline: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail
primary_source.content: Chicago's largest jail, and the largest single use jail in America, is Cook County. In 2023 it saw a spike in overdose deaths. The facility, which averages one or two overdose deaths a year, lost eight inmates that year to fatal seizures. Security footage shows prisoners spasming and collapsing. Traditional drugs were usually brought into the jail in body cavities, so the jail had the same body scanners you find at airports to prevent that happening. However, a new way of drugs entering the prison was uncovered. Drugs were being mailed into the jail soaked in the paper of the pages of books and in letters. The BBC's Quentin Sommerville joined corrections officers at Cook County as they prepared for an early morning raid on the jail's high security D block. To understand the challenge that authorities face in tackling the problem the BBC interviewed a former inmate and dealer, who explained how synthetic drugs can be made in the US using household ingredients and how this could change the demand for drugs from outside of the country.

brief_bullets: A tragic road accident occurred in Hayathnagar, Hyderabad, when a Mahindra Thar SUV collided with a scooter, resulting in the immediate deaths of two individuals. The victims, who were traveling on the two-wheeler, succumbed to their injuries at the scene, while a three-year-old girl accompanying them sustained significant injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital for urgent medical care. Local law enforcement officials have initiated a formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the collision, focusing on potential reckless driving or negligence by the SUV operator. This incident has reignited public discourse regarding road safety standards and the increasing prevalence of high-speed vehicle accidents involving heavy SUVs on urban arterial roads. Authorities are currently reviewing surveillance footage and gathering witness testimonies to determine the precise sequence of events that led to this fatal encounter.
why_it_matters_bullets: The incident highlights the growing public safety concerns surrounding the proliferation of large, high-performance SUVs in dense urban environments and underscores the urgent need for stricter traffic enforcement to mitigate fatal road accidents.

stories.primary_headline: Man, 80, who died in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond named

primary_source.headline: Man, 80, who died in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond named
primary_source.content: Ian Haggis - pictured when he was younger - died when the light aircraft crashed near Loch Lomond He and a 16-year-old boy died when their plane came down near Loch Lomond. The teenager's identity has not been released. The pair had flown out from Glasgow Airport at 16:17 and stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of the village of Drymen near Stirling. Emergency services were called to the crash at about 16:45 on Friday. Both of them were pronounced dead at the scene. Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) carries out its inquiries.

stories.primary_headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives

primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.

stories.primary_headline: From Gulshan Kumar to Tiger Shroff, Bollywood figures in the crosshairs

primary_source.headline: From Gulshan Kumar to Tiger Shroff, Bollywood figures in the crosshairs
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Actor Tiger Shroff, who escaped unhurt after three rounds were fired at him in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday, is the latest Bollywood personality to have been the target of shootings over the years.In February this year, five rounds were fired outside the Juhu residence of filmmaker Rohit Shetty. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing.In April 2024, two bike-borne men fired five rounds outside actor Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai’s Bandra area.The Mumbai Police arrested many suspects linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. A trial against the five accused - Vicky Gupta, Sagar Pal, Harpal Singh, Sonukumar Bishnoi, and Mohammad Rafiq Choudhari - is underway. The sixth accused, Anuj Kumar Thapan, died in police custody in May 2024.In January 2000, filmmaker Rakesh Roshan was shot and injured in an assassination attempt in Santacruz area of Mumbai, just a week after the release of his blockbuster film Kaho Naa Pyaar Hai.Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt as suspected Lawrence Bishnoi gang members open fireTwo assailants fired multiple shots at him. One bullet hit his left arm and another grazed his chest.In August 1997, T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar was shot dead outside the Jiteshwar Mahadev Temple in Mumbai’s Andheri area. He was shot 16 times by the assailants.Comedian Kapil Sharma's restaurant, Kap's Café, located in Canada’s British Columbia province, was targeted in three separate shooting incidents between July and October last year.

stories.primary_headline: FSSAI urges safe transport and storage of perishable foods to prevent spoilage

primary_source.headline: FSSAI urges safe transport and storage of perishable foods to prevent spoilage
primary_source.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has directed all food business operators to ensure that perishable food items like khoa, paneer, meat, and fish are transported safely in hygienic conditions.&nbsp;“Owing to their perishable nature, these food items are highly susceptible to microbial growth and spoilage if not maintained under appropriate temperature conditions,” the FSSAI advisory dated October 15 stated.&nbsp;In the advisory, the food regulatory authority revealed that perishable food items like khoa, paneer, meat, etc are not handled, stored, or transported under appropriate temperature conditions. This should be maintained throughout the supply chain, from procurement till delivery to the end consumer. Subjecting these food items to temperature abuse may adversely affect food safety and public health and constitutes non-compliance with the hygiene and sanitary requirements prescribed by the FSSAI.&nbsp;FSSAI issues an advisory on handling, storage, and transportation of perishable foods like khoas, paneer, meat, and fish under controlled temperature conditions throughout the supply chain.  
FBOs must ensure strict adherence to hygiene and temperature standards 
#FSSAIAdvisory https://t.co/U4XZc09Xf4&mdash; FSSAI (@fssaiindia) October 18, 2026
 FSSAI proposes banning addition of fructose, sucrose in baby food productsFSSAI proposes stricter front-of-pack warning label rules for packaged foods after backlashThe regulator further added that FBOs should use only food-grade packaging materials and suitable secondary packaging. The use of gunny bags or other non-food-grade coverings for packing or transporting compromises product safety and should be avoided.&nbsp;Additionally, food businesses should also ensure that necessary measures are taken to protect products from dust, moisture, pests, physical damage and cross-contamination during storage, loading, unloading and transportation.&nbsp;They must also maintain proper records and traceability of consignments and produce invoices or other relevant documents whenever demanded by the competent authority.

#FSSAIAdvisory https://t.co/U4XZc09Xf4&mdash; FSSAI (@fssaiindia) October 18, 2026
 FSSAI proposes banning addition of fructose, sucrose in baby food productsFSSAI proposes stricter front-of-pack warning label rules for packaged foods after backlashThe regulator further added that FBOs should use only food-grade packaging materials and suitable secondary packaging. The use of gunny bags or other non-food-grade coverings for packing or transporting compromises product safety and should be avoided.&nbsp;Additionally, food businesses should also ensure that necessary measures are taken to protect products from dust, moisture, pests, physical damage and cross-contamination during storage, loading, unloading and transportation.&nbsp;They must also maintain proper records and traceability of consignments and produce invoices or other relevant documents whenever demanded by the competent authority.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes

primary_source.headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
primary_source.content: Ranipet (Tamil Nadu): Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday.He was 75.Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17.His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director.Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry.Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur.‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva (1950-2026): The maestro who took gaana to the masses Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government’s Public Works Department (PWD).He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time.'Manasukketha Maharasa' (1989), starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim.Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the ‘gaana’ genre into mainstream Tamil cinema.Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai.He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers.Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films ‘Annamalai’, ‘Baashha’ and ‘Arunachalam’, and the Kamal Haasan outings ‘Avvai Shanmugi’, ‘Pammal K Sambandam’ and ‘Panchathanthiram’.His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu.

stories.primary_headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues

primary_source.headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: ‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolition

primary_source.headline: ‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolition
primary_source.content: WBO heavyweight champion targets big paydays against Hrgovic, Kabayel and Itauma after second round winThirty minutes after Daniel Dubois had dismantled Fabio Wardley in less than two rounds on Saturday night, his promoter Frank Warren shook his head in slight awe as he described the intensity before the annihilation: “I went in the dressing room beforehand like I normally do and I couldn’t have a conversation with Daniel because he was so zoned in and focused. It showed when he got in the ring. He went out there on a seek-and-destroy mission.”Dubois resembled a much bigger and heavier version of a young Mike Tyson as, wearing black trunks and a black cape, he walked to the ring with intense purpose. There was not a flicker of emotion as he marched quickly towards Wardley for their WBO world title rematch. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’

primary_source.headline: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’
primary_source.content: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as AdeleBorn in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge. After a stint as lead singer of the punk band the Wigs, he became an apprentice at Harefield Pottery in London. He went on to set up his own company, and created pots and homewares for retailers including Conran, Habitat and Laura Ashley, before developing his signature Word range. He has been a judge on The Great Pottery Throw Down since it started in 2015. His new book, Firing Earth: An Unexpected History of Pots and Potters, is published on 22 October.This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

For democracy activists, that’s a disasterMarco Rubio was once adamant that the US had to do everything in its power to end what he described as the “ethnic cleansing” of the Rohingya in Myanmar. In a 2017 letter he signed along with 20 other US senators, Rubio called for “strong multilateral sanctions against specific senior Burmese military officials associated with the gross human rights abuses”. Those responsible for the atrocities should be prosecuted, he argued.In the years since, the Myanmar military’s crimes have only increased. What was then deemed ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya is now widely viewed, including by the US, as genocide. What little democracy existed in Myanmar was eradicated in 2021 when Aung San Suu Kyi was arrested and imprisoned and her party’s election victory overturned, and the military took full control. primary_source.headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene. Continue reading...

brief_bullets: A tragic incident occurred in Kerala when a local man suffered a fatal heart attack while harvesting ice apples from a 60-foot-tall palmyra palm tree. The individual, who had ascended the towering palm to collect the seasonal fruit, failed to descend as expected, prompting concerned local residents to investigate his prolonged absence. Upon climbing the tree to check on his status, bystanders discovered that the man had succumbed to a cardiac event while still positioned at the summit. Despite immediate efforts by the community to retrieve him and provide assistance, he was confirmed dead by the time he was successfully lowered to the ground. This unfortunate event highlights the inherent physical risks associated with traditional agricultural practices in the region, where laborers often navigate extreme heights without specialized safety equipment or professional oversight to supplement their manual harvesting methods.
why_it_matters_bullets: This incident underscores the urgent need for improved occupational safety standards and the implementation of protective gear for traditional agricultural workers who face significant physical hazards in rural economies. It also serves as a sobering reminder of the vulnerability of aging or health-compromised laborers performing high-altitude tasks without medical monitoring.

stories.primary_headline: Less plastic, more pujo vibes: Assam town gives Durga Puja a 'carbon-neutral' twist

primary_source.headline: Less plastic, more pujo vibes: Assam town gives Durga Puja a 'carbon-neutral' twist
primary_source.content: Durga Puja celebrations mean glitzy pandals, excessive lighting, high-decibel music and many more attractions.But several committees organising the annual Durga Puja in Kokrajhar town in western Assam, the district headquarters of the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), have pitched in to adopt the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations by planting trees, reducing the use of non-biodegradable items and even lowering the volume of music systems to check sound pollution.A set of dos and don'ts were proposed by the Kokrajhar district administration for nearly 200 Durga Puja committees in the town as part of efforts to popularise the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations.“We proposed the idea as part of our efforts to have environmentally responsible festivities while preserving the religious and cultural essence of the festival. It is very nice to see that nearly 50 per cent of the committees have responded very positively by significantly reducing the use of plastic items, planting trees and even controlling the volume of music systems,” Kokrajhar District Commissioner Pankaj Chakravarty told DH over the phone on Sunday. Kokrajhar is situated about 200 km west of Guwahati.Durga Puja celebrations began on Friday and will continue till Wednesday, following which the Durga idols will be immersed in rivers.With a population of nearly 35,000 (2011 Census), Kokrajhar Municipal town has diverse communities, including Bodos, Bengalis, Assamese, Rabhas, Nepalis, Adivasis, Saranias and others, each peacefully celebrating their own festivals.Lotus theme, red-and-white decor to mark Durga Puja in BengaluruCarbon-neutral celebrationsUnder the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations, the district administration proposed several measures, such as encouraging the use of locally available and reusable materials, including bamboo, jute, recycled paper and other environmentally responsible alternatives, for pandals and decorations; promoting idols made from natural clay and other biodegradable materials, with non-toxic colours, to minimise environmental pollution, particularly during immersion; tree plantation; the use of solar energy and LED lights; responsible sound management; and encouraging waste segregation, responsible disposal and recycling, among other measures.“This is an encouraging beginning. The drive is resulting in public awareness, with the concept being shared by many on social media platforms. We hope more and more Durga Puja committees will accept and implement the concept gradually in the years ahead to make environmental awareness an integral part of the festivities, encouraging every puja committee and community to contribute towards a cleaner and greener Kokrajhar and Assam at large,” Chakravarty said.“The message is simple: let our devotion to Maa Durga inspire us to protect Mother Earth. Through collective efforts by puja committees, citizens, community organisations and the District Administration, Kokrajhar aspires to set a meaningful example of how faith, tradition and sustainability can go hand in hand, contributing to a greener future for the Bodoland Territorial Region and Assam as a whole.”

sources.headline: Less plastic, more pujo vibes: Assam town gives Durga Puja a 'carbon-neutral' twist
sources.content: Durga Puja celebrations mean glitzy pandals, excessive lighting, high-decibel music and many more attractions.But several committees organising the annual Durga Puja in Kokrajhar town in western Assam, the district headquarters of the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), have pitched in to adopt the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations by planting trees, reducing the use of non-biodegradable items and even lowering the volume of music systems to check sound pollution.A set of dos and don'ts were proposed by the Kokrajhar district administration for nearly 200 Durga Puja committees in the town as part of efforts to popularise the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations.“We proposed the idea as part of our efforts to have environmentally responsible festivities while preserving the religious and cultural essence of the festival. It is very nice to see that nearly 50 per cent of the committees have responded very positively by significantly reducing the use of plastic items, planting trees and even controlling the volume of music systems,” Kokrajhar District Commissioner Pankaj Chakravarty told DH over the phone on Sunday. Kokrajhar is situated about 200 km west of Guwahati.Durga Puja celebrations began on Friday and will continue till Wednesday, following which the Durga idols will be immersed in rivers.With a population of nearly 35,000 (2011 Census), Kokrajhar Municipal town has diverse communities, including Bodos, Bengalis, Assamese, Rabhas, Nepalis, Adivasis, Saranias and others, each peacefully celebrating their own festivals.Lotus theme, red-and-white decor to mark Durga Puja in BengaluruCarbon-neutral celebrationsUnder the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations, the district administration proposed several measures, such as encouraging the use of locally available and reusable materials, including bamboo, jute, recycled paper and other environmentally responsible alternatives, for pandals and decorations; promoting idols made from natural clay and other biodegradable materials, with non-toxic colours, to minimise environmental pollution, particularly during immersion; tree plantation; the use of solar energy and LED lights; responsible sound management; and encouraging waste segregation, responsible disposal and recycling, among other measures.“This is an encouraging beginning. The drive is resulting in public awareness, with the concept being shared by many on social media platforms. We hope more and more Durga Puja committees will accept and implement the concept gradually in the years ahead to make environmental awareness an integral part of the festivities, encouraging every puja committee and community to contribute towards a cleaner and greener Kokrajhar and Assam at large,” Chakravarty said.“The message is simple: let our devotion to Maa Durga inspire us to protect Mother Earth. Through collective efforts by puja committees, citizens, community organisations and the District Administration, Kokrajhar aspires to set a meaningful example of how faith, tradition and sustainability can go hand in hand, contributing to a greener future for the Bodoland Territorial Region and Assam as a whole.”
