stories.primary_headline: Reports of sale false and misleading, says Bhilai Steel Plant amid Congress alleging Adani visit

primary_source.headline: Reports of sale false and misleading, says Bhilai Steel Plant amid Congress alleging Adani visit
primary_source.content: Durg: Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP), a Chhattisgarh-based unit of state-run Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), on Sunday dismissed reports about its proposed sale as "false and misleading", the assertion coming amid allegations from the Congress that the Adani Group was planning to visit the facility.The BSP is located in Bhilai city in Durg district.In a statement, the BSP said the Ministry of Steel has refuted the claims through its official social media handle, while the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check had also confirmed that the reports are false.The plant appealed to its employees, stakeholders and the people of Chhattisgarh not to believe or circulate unverified information and urged them to rely on official and authenticated sources."BSP is not merely an industrial establishment; it is an integral part of Chhattisgarh's identity, pride and industrial legacy. Since its inception, the plant has played a pivotal role in the state's industrial development by generating employment, supporting ancillary industries and contributing to the livelihoods of thousands of families," it said.Its legacy and contribution have made it a source of pride for the people of Chhattisgarh, the statement asserted.Karnataka government to negotiate with Adani over tunnel road costAs a major unit of SAIL, the Bhilai Steel Plant continues to contribute to the growth of the country's steel sector and strengthen India's industrial capabilities, the statement said.The BSP urged the people to refrain from spreading misinformation that could create unnecessary confusion among employees, their families and the people of Chhattisgarh.The clarification came after former Chhattisgarh chief minister and senior Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel alleged that Adani was likely to visit the plant.In a post on X on October 14, Baghel said, "It has come to light that Adani is set to visit the Bhilai Steel Plant - our BSP. Do you understand the implications of Adani's visit to the BSP? It means that Narendra Modi who is spearheading a campaign to sell off the nation, has now set his sights on our BSP. And his favored buyer is coming to conduct an inspection"."Modi ji should realize that the BSP is the soul of Chhattisgarh. And we, the people of Chhattisgarh, will not allow it to be sold under any circumstances. Not under any circumstances," Baghel added.Chhattisgarh BJP leaders should also understand that BSP is not for sale, Baghel had said.Meanwhile, Congress's Bhilai unit president Mukesh Chandrakar, in a statement on Sunday, said reports about the plant's possible privatisation and the Adani Group's alleged visit had triggered anger in the industrial town.The reports had created apprehensions among employees, local shopkeepers and residents over job security, minimum wages for workers and the future of the plant's township, he claimed.

brief_bullets: The Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP), a critical unit of the state-run Steel Authority of India Limited, has formally dismissed circulating reports regarding its potential privatization as entirely false and misleading. This clarification follows intense political controversy ignited by former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel, who alleged that the Adani Group was planning an inspection visit to the facility as a precursor to a government-led sale. In response, the Ministry of Steel and the Press Information Bureau have officially refuted these claims, emphasizing that the plant remains a vital pillar of India's industrial legacy and regional economic stability. The BSP management has urged its workforce and the local community to disregard unverified rumors, which had previously sparked significant anxiety regarding job security and the future of the township. By addressing these allegations directly, the plant aims to stabilize its operations and reaffirm its status as a cornerstone of Chhattisgarh’s industrial identity.
why_it_matters_bullets: The incident highlights the heightened sensitivity surrounding the privatization of state-owned assets in India, where political rhetoric can rapidly destabilize industrial morale and local economic sentiment. It underscores the necessity for government entities to proactively manage misinformation to prevent labor unrest and maintain public trust in strategic national infrastructure.

stories.primary_headline: Mangaluru man arrested in stabbing incident

primary_source.headline: Mangaluru man arrested in stabbing incident
primary_source.content: Mangaluru: A 28-year-old man was taken into custody on Sunday in connection with a stabbing incident reported at Pallamajalu Junction in Bantwal taluk on Saturday night.According to the complainant, Lokesh, 27, a resident of B Mooda village in Bantwal, alleged that the accused, Ajith Kumar Shetty, a resident of Pallamajalu in Bantwal taluk, had borrowed money from his brother Uday. When Uday repeatedly asked him to return the money, the accused allegedly told him on Saturday that he would repay it and asked him to come to Pallamajalu.Uday went to Pallamajalu Junction to collect the money and also asked his brother Lokesh to come there. When Lokesh reached the spot, he allegedly witnessed Ajith attacking Uday with a knife. When Lokesh attempted to intervene, the accused allegedly chased him. Rights must anchor the rules of arrestLocal residents subsequently took Uday to the Bantwal government hospital for treatment. He was later shifted to a hospital in Mangaluru for further treatment.A case has been registered at Bantwal Town Police Station under Sections 118(2), 109(1) and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.The police took Ajith Kumar Shetty into custody for investigation. He will be questioned further and produced before the court.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: I saw rioting, looting, above all, anger. If French leaders think more violence will solve this, they’re mistaken | Oliver Haynes

primary_source.headline: I saw rioting, looting, above all, anger. If French leaders think more violence will solve this, they’re mistaken | Oliver Haynes
primary_source.content: It’s a perfect storm of protesters with heartfelt grievances and others set on conflict. The key here is the sense of betrayal that united them on the streetsThe first thing I learned on the streets of Paris this weekend is that there is no arguing with teargas. I arrived at Place de la République just after 1pm yesterday. The mood was festive until police started firing volleys of teargas into the square from Rue du Faubourg-du-Temple.I didn’t see the inciting incident – if there even was one – and tried walking into the cloud of CS gas hanging in the air. It was impossible. The gas clings to your nose and burns your eyes, and you quickly start struggling to breathe. I retreated towards the Boulevard de Magenta, blinking furiously to stop the stinging.Oliver Haynes is a journalist and co-host of Sacré Bleu: the French presidential election podcastDo you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? stories.primary_headline: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III

primary_source.headline: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III
primary_source.content: Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysisDramatic new evidence concludes that the play Edward III should be added to William Shakespeare’s canon, and also that it was a major collaboration with his contemporary rival Christopher Marlowe.The history was published anonymously in 1596, and it has long been thought that Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Private citizens can file criminal complaints against candidates for submitting false affidavits with their nomination papers, the Supreme Court has ruled, clarifying that no prior sanction or complaint from the Election Commission or any public servant is required.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that an offence under Section 125-A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, does not fall within the restrictive ambit of Section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. EC-SIR row | ‘Undermining EC, Supreme Court is not a right’: Harvard scholars warns against erosion of public trust in IndiaThe non-obstante clause in Section 125-A and the deliberate legislative omission to include it in Section 195 CrPC mean courts can take cognizance of such complaints lodged by private persons under Section 200 CrPC, the court said.The ruling came in an appeal filed by Rajkumar Madki challenging a March 7, 2025, judgment of the Karnataka High Court. The High Court had quashed Madki’s August 2023 private complaint against Dr Shailendra Beldale, the MLA from Bidar, alleging that the legislator had given a false residential address in the affidavit accompanying his 2023 nomination papers.The October 16, 2026 decision settles a substantial question of law of general public importance that had not been previously decided by the court.The High Court had held that only the Election Commission could complain of an offence under Section 125-A and that a voter’s remedy was limited to an election petition. The Supreme Court disagreed on the legal point, observing that courts cannot expand the list of offences requiring a public servant’s complaint by implication.“The prohibition on a court taking cognizance… is restricted to the offences specifically enumerated therein,” the bench said. Supreme Court seeks replies from CEC Gyanesh Kumar, others on plea filed by Rahul Gandhi, oppn leadersIt noted that Section 125-A is of relatively recent origin and that Parliament could have amended Section 195 CrPC if it intended to restrict such prosecutions. Guidelines or press notes issued by the Election Commission, the court added, cannot bind judicial interpretation of the statute.Despite upholding the maintainability of private complaints in principle, the apex court declined to revive the specific case against Beldale, represented by senior advocate Anand Sanjay M Nuli. It found that the documents on record effectively rebutted the allegation of false declaration of residence and that the prospect of conviction was remote. Continuing the trial, the court said, would only waste judicial time.The High Court’s order quashing the proceedings was therefore left undisturbed, but on different grounds. The Supreme Court made it clear that magistrates retain full powers to deal with frivolous or harassing complaints if any are filed in future.

stories.primary_headline: Zubeen Garg murder case: Assam CID to challenge bail for bandmate, cousin in SC

primary_source.headline: Zubeen Garg murder case: Assam CID to challenge bail for bandmate, cousin in SC
primary_source.content: Guwahati: Amid sharp public reactions to the bail granted to two accused in the alleged murder case of Zubeen Garg, the Assam CID on Sunday said it had decided to challenge the bail orders in the Supreme Court.Special Director General of Police, CID, Munna Prasad Gupta said the decision to move the Supreme Court challenging the bail granted by the Gauhati High Court to two accused, female bandmate Amritprabha Mahanta and cousin Sandipan Garg, was taken after examining the bail orders.Mahanta was granted bail on October 9, while Garg, a suspended Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), got bail from the High Court on Friday. Both were present when cultural icon Zubeen Garg died at sea in Singapore on September 19 last year. Garg drowned during a yacht party.Assam Advocate General Devajit Saikia told reporters that the decision to challenge the bail orders was taken after loopholes were detected in the High Court orders granting bail to Amritprabha and Sandipan.Two of Zubeen's personal security officers (PSOs) were also granted bail by the High Court earlier.Following the bail orders, many expressed doubts over Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that Garg was murdered by the accused and his assurance of justice.Zubeen Garg death case: After bandmate, cousin Sandipan gets bailThe influential All Assam Students' Union even demanded that the state government challenge the bail orders in the Supreme Court.The three remaining accused, Shyamkanu Mahanta, Garg's manager Siddharth Sharma, and Shekhar Jyoti Goswami, a drummer in Garg's band, are still in judicial custody. Garg was in Singapore to attend the Northeast India Festival organised by Shyamkanu Mahanta's firm.The trial in the case, however, is underway in a fast-track court.Although Garg's death was initially suspected to be a drowning mishap, CM Sarma claimed that he was murdered by a few people and that others had assisted them.Sarma even told the Assembly that it was a "plain and simple murder case". A coroner's court in Singapore, however, ruled in March this year that Garg's death was due to drowning and that no foul play could be established.Lakhs of his fans, who were emotional and angry, took to the streets and demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible for the alleged crime.

stories.primary_headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters

primary_source.headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi Police has registered at least 10 FIRs and arrested five people in connection with alleged harassment and assaults on protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with several social media posts accusing right-wing activists of targeting demonstrators, officials said on Sunday.The cases were registered between October 11 and 14 at Connaught Place and Kamla Market police stations after videos and posts highlighting alleged attacks on protesters circulated on social media.At least five people have been arrested in two separate cases, a senior police officer said.According to the police, an FIR was registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 in connection with an incident flagged through social media handles.Delhi Police registers four FIRs against 'rumour-mongers', Pak social media handles under scannerGaurav was arrested in the case, while efforts are underway to trace his alleged accomplices.A group of men was seen assaulting a protester while daring others to call them "cockroaches". One of the men was also heard threatening to beat up anyone who spoke against the prime minister or the police.In another case, registered at Kamla Market police station on October 11, four people were arrested after a video purportedly showing individuals harassing and assaulting protesters went viral.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and initiated legal action against those allegedly involved.The list of cases also includes multiple FIRs registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 and 14 over incidents highlighted in social media posts and videos. spreading 'rumours'Several social media posts have alleged that right-wing activists assaulted or harassed protesters during the demonstrations.The footage and allegations are being examined by police as they work to identify the people involved and establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents.The police action comes amid a wider scrutiny of online content related to the protests, with authorities also investigating posts allegedly circulating misinformation, rumours and fabricated videos.Some social media accounts have shared claims of police brutality against demonstrators, which investigators are examining to establish their authenticity.In one of the cases, police have sought information from social media platform X to identify a user accused of uploading videos that they suspect were fabricated and circulated to disrupt public order.Police have identified more than 37 social media accounts, including over 17 allegedly linked to right-wing groups, for purportedly circulating misleading content related to the protests, a source in the police said.Takedown notices have been issued to more than 17 handles, including those linked to right-wing groups, and action has been initiated under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and other laws for allegedly inciting people and disrupting law and order, they said.Some right-wing accounts allegedly shared posts and reels targeting protesters and presenting the demonstrations in a misleading manner, while other users circulated videos purportedly showing police brutality against demonstrators.Investigators are examining the content to verify its authenticity and identify those responsible, the officials added.The protests in the national capital have been organised over demands for Kumar's resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise. Further investigation in the cases is underway.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants
primary_source.content: Mysuru: After 48 days of training, the final round of the last two days' of rehearsal began for all 13 Dasara Elephants infront of Mysuru Palace on Sunday morning.&nbsp;Flanked by Cauvery and Roopa, lead Elephant Prashantha, who has been finalised for carrying golden howdah, marched towards the podium.&nbsp;Chief Conservator of Forest Mysuru circle S S Ravishankar, DCF, Wildlife&nbsp;I B Prabhugowda, Mysuru city police commissioner Seema Latkar offered floral benediction as part of the rehearsal. On Wednesday Chief Minister D K Shivakumar will offer floral benediction to the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari which will be housed in golden howdah, mounted on Prashantha at the end of Dasara Jamboo Savari procession on Vijayadashami on October 21. This year, even Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Kerala who are expected to participate in the procession, are also likely to accompany CM D K Shivakumar on the podium, according to sources.Mysuru Dasara: 'Prashantha' to be lead elephant carrying golden howdah in Vijayadashami processionThe Police band led by band master B Manjunath, played even the national song-Vande Matharam for the first time along with the national Anthem during the floral benediction. Mounted cops&nbsp;also joined the rehearsal.&nbsp;Parade commander K N Suresh, Assistant Parade commander&nbsp;Sharanappa Sasanur&nbsp;accompanied the howdah Elephant.&nbsp;Prior to that, Abhimanyu marched as the&nbsp;Nishaane Elephant leading the procession at the forefront. Gopi followed him as the Nauphath Elephant. Mahendra and Lakshmi; Srirama, Chithra and Sugreeva; Srikanta and Ekalavya marched as Saalanes in three batches.&nbsp;Veteran Abhimanyu who carried golden howdah for six years till last year, has been relieved from this prime duty this year as he has turned 60 years of age. Hence Prashantha, Mahendra, Dhananjaya, Ekalavya and Sugreeva were trained to carry the weight equivalent to golden howdah. After the completion of their training on Tuesday, Prashantha was finalised on Wednesday to carry golden howdah in the procession.&nbsp;Dasara elephants, horses acquainted with cannon fire shotsThe first batch of nine Dasara elephants arrived at the Aranya Bhavan in Mysuru after a grand Gajapayana event at Veeranahosahalli in Hunsur taluk on August 26. They were accorded a grand traditional welcome on the Palace premises on August 28 and have been housed there since then. Their weight was checked, and they are being treated to a special nutritious diet to maintain their strength and build stamina for the big day, from August 30. Their training began on August 30. They were familiarised with the crowd, and the procession route from Palace to Government Ayurveda college circle till September 4. From September 5, they were familiarised with the entire procession route till Bannimantap ground. Training to carry weight began on September 6. Elephants Sugreeva, Roopa and Chaithra arrived in the second batch on September 13. Training to carry wooden howdah began on September 25. They were acquainted with cannon fire shots from brass barrels on October 7, 9 and 12, as 21 Cannon shots will be fired during floral benediction to Goddess at the end of procession on Vijayadashami.&nbsp;

primary_source.headline: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
primary_source.content: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriageMost couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite.Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, 4 sureties rejected

primary_source.headline: CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, 4 sureties rejected
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The bail hearing of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka was "delayed" on Sunday as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) did not arrive at the scheduled time, activist Ratna Singh said and alleged that four sureties had been rejected on "vague" grounds.Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after they entered Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, by scaling its locked gates. The CJP leaders maintained that they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.In a post on X, Singh said she had been at the police station since 11 am, while the hearing was scheduled for noon. She said the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP/SEM) had not arrived at the Mandir Marg police station by 4.42 pm.CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde under preventive arrest; likely to be produced before magistrate"This is really concerning. They have rejected 4 sureties till now on vague reasons. They have made people who have FIRs against them for being part of protest as people having criminal antecedents (sic)," Singh alleged.There was no response from police on the allegations.In another post, Singh said, "Unfurling the Indian National Flag is not a crime, and the boys should not remain in custody due to procedural delays."Questioning the functioning of the SEM courts in the national capital, Singh said higher courts had asked authorities to follow the hierarchy and alleged an "absolute misuse of power".On Saturday, the CJP said in a post on X that it had consulted senior advocate Kapil Sibal and warned of legal action if Das and Ranka were not released by Sunday."If Ashu and Saurav are not released by tomorrow, we will pursue legal action against all those who deliberately ensured that they continue to be in illegal custody, especially when they have not committed nor charged with any offence," the outfit had said."The deliberate use of delaying tactics to keep them behind bars cannot go unchallenged. Those responsible will be held accountable," it added.The outfit has been protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the exercise threatens voters' rights.

stories.primary_headline: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting

primary_source.headline: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting
primary_source.content: The officer was shot after approaching two people in Angel Row, Nottingham Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday. The officer is in a stable condition in hospital, where he is receiving treatment for a wound to his foot, the force added. Detectives said a man and a woman had fled the scene and that a firearm, which could be seen within the cordon, had been found. Angel Row is currently closed and a large police scene remains in place. Police cars are parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops, and orange traffic cones have been laid out alongside items left on the road.

stories.primary_headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction

primary_source.headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state. According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of&nbsp; 30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed. The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation. Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments. The silt accumulation in the water bodies, which reduced the water holding capacity, has been found to be a reason for flash floods in the state. Keralam, which requires up to 30 million metric tonnes of sand annually, has been highly dependent on Tamil Nadu for rocks to sand. Hence the restriction by the neighbouring state has led to an acute scarcity in Keralam, which already led to almost three times cost escalation. Major infrastructure projects like the ongoing expansion of Vizhinjam international seaport and national highway were reportedly feeling the heat. Desilting of the water bodies is hence considered to have multiple benefits ranging from addressing construction material shortage to flood mitigation. Tamil Nadu bans transportation of rough stones to other states; Kerala seeks review The state government was forced to impose a ban on river sand mining in 2016 in view of the massive unregulated sand mining which even diverted the direction of flow of rivers at many places. Hence, the state has been depending on manufactured sand for construction. The stringent regulations for quarries have also&nbsp; led to the number of quarries coming down around 220 from 3800 ten years back, according to the Keralam Mining and Crushing Owners Association. Even as the state government initiated steps for desilting at a couple of dams like the Mangalam dam in Palakkad and introduced stringent norms for regulated river sand mining following the 2018-19 floods, those steps went into troubled waters&nbsp; owing to allegations of over exploitation and ecological concerns. Industry sources said that since the chances of Tamil Nadu easing the restrictions was remote, the state government should proactively take steps to address the crisis.&nbsp; Natural river sand offers a better construction quality than manufactured sand. Hence the government should take steps for regulated desilting and river sand mining," said Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India general convener general. However, environmental expert V Subashchandrabose points out that even as scientific desilting and river sand mining could be allowed, the state should popularise alternative&nbsp; construction methods that could reduce the dependence on natural resources.

stories.primary_headline: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary

primary_source.headline: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary
primary_source.content: No patient should be treated in a corridor, Yvette Cooper says Yvette Cooper told the BBC there would be new standards for caring for children in A&E in England, with figures collected on corridor care by age for the first time. She was speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg where the programme highlighted the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts who died in a hospital corridor in 2024. The health secretary has announced £140m to improve urgent care in England ahead of what she said would be a "more difficult" winter than usual. The government has already pledged to end corridor care for all patients by the end of this parliament, and now Cooper has said eradicating it for children would be prioritised. Corridor care refers to patients receiving treatment or waiting in corridors, waiting rooms or other hospital areas due to a lack of appropriate space.

stories.primary_headline: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …

primary_source.headline: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …
primary_source.content: Cool, juicy pears, cold ice-cream, hot chocolate sauce and a crunchy garnish – the perfect puddingIt’s always slightly embarrassing to realise that you’ve missed a pop culture reference, even if it’s 162 years old, so I won’t dwell on the fact that until last week I was unaware of the existence of Offenbach’s 1864 operetta about Helen of Troy, La Belle Hélène, after which today’s dish is named. In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider.Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire, none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. As Nigel Slater observes in Tender: Volume 2, “The marriage of pears and chocolate is extraordinary. It is as if they were made for each other.” This, I think, is the duo at its “most sumptuous”. Continue reading...

In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider.Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire, none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. sources.headline: Opinion: Blog: Kolkata Didn't Learn From 2015. Eleven Years Later, It Proved To Be Fatal
sources.content: The City of Joy isn't a stranger to crowd control. Be it during Pujo or Christmas at Park Street, Eden Gardens cricket matches, or Derbies between Mohun Bagan and East Bengal. But during Pujo, the entire city is on alert.

brief_bullets: Kolkata, a city historically accustomed to managing massive crowds during high-profile events like Durga Pujo, Christmas celebrations, and intense sporting derbies, faces renewed scrutiny following a tragic failure in crowd management. Despite the city's extensive experience with large-scale public gatherings, recent events suggest that systemic vulnerabilities persist, echoing the catastrophic lapses observed during the 2015 incidents. Critics argue that the municipal and law enforcement authorities have failed to institutionalize the lessons learned over the past decade, leading to preventable fatalities that undermine the city's reputation for safe public festivities. This recurring inability to implement robust safety protocols during peak periods highlights a dangerous complacency within urban planning and emergency response frameworks. As the city continues to host millions of visitors annually, the persistent gap between operational preparedness and the reality of crowd dynamics remains a critical concern for public safety officials and local governance. The failure to address long-standing crowd control deficiencies threatens the viability of Kolkata’s major cultural economy and exposes the city to significant legal and reputational risks. It underscores a broader need for modernized, data-driven infrastructure to manage urban density in rapidly growing metropolitan centers.

brief_bullets: Donald Trump’s ambitious proposal to redevelop the historic East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C., into a championship-level course has encountered a significant regulatory roadblock. The project, which aimed to transform the public recreational space into an exclusive enclave for elites, necessitated the removal of over 430 mature trees to accommodate redesigned fairways and greens. Critics and environmental advocates have scrutinized the plan, arguing that the clearing of such a substantial canopy would irreparably damage the landscape of the capital’s public park system. For the time being, the initiative has been effectively halted, preventing the immediate destruction of the site's natural infrastructure. This standoff highlights the ongoing tension between private commercial interests in luxury sports development and the preservation of public land, reflecting broader debates over the privatization of urban spaces in the nation's capital. The project’s stall underscores the significant legal and environmental hurdles facing high-profile development plans on public land, signaling that even influential figures must navigate rigorous federal oversight and public opposition. It serves as a litmus test for the future of urban land use in Washington, D.C., where the balance between elite recreational expansion and public environmental stewardship remains a contentious policy battleground.

stories.primary_headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

primary_source.headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

sources.headline: G7 to launch exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks

brief_bullets: The Group of Seven (G7) nations have announced a coordinated initiative to launch large-scale simulation exercises designed to bolster collective defenses against sophisticated cyberattacks powered by artificial intelligence. This strategic move, spearheaded by member nations, aims to address the escalating threat landscape where malicious actors increasingly leverage generative AI to automate phishing campaigns, develop polymorphic malware, and execute high-velocity data breaches. By conducting these rigorous stress tests, the G7 intends to harmonize incident response protocols, enhance cross-border information sharing, and identify critical vulnerabilities within shared digital infrastructure. This collaborative framework reflects a growing consensus among global leaders that traditional cybersecurity measures are insufficient against the speed and adaptability of AI-driven threats. Ultimately, the exercises serve as a proactive mechanism to ensure that democratic economies remain resilient against state-sponsored and criminal cyber operations that threaten global financial stability and national security. This initiative marks a pivotal shift toward proactive, multilateral cyber-defense, signaling that G7 nations are prioritizing the standardization of AI-security protocols to prevent systemic digital collapse. It establishes a new geopolitical benchmark for how advanced economies must integrate defensive AI capabilities to counter the asymmetric advantages currently enjoyed by sophisticated cyber adversaries.

stories.primary_headline: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat

primary_source.headline: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
primary_source.content: What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end. After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula. This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family. It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC. The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size. "In winter, they would keep them at the shipyard. When summer came, they would bring them out and move them to Kim Jong Un's villa or towards Kalma, and use them for swimming and recreation," says Ri Jong Ho.

stories.primary_headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

primary_source.headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
primary_source.content: Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude  and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.

Authorities continue to monitor inflow and outflow rates closely to manage the state's water security, particularly as agricultural demands fluctuate throughout the season. sources.content: The KPCC president denies funding CJP protests but justifies what he calls his party’s logistical support to the agitating youth

brief_bullets: Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President B.K. Hariprasad has launched a scathing critique of the central government, accusing it of systemic negligence in strengthening the national education sector. Amidst ongoing political tensions, Hariprasad categorically denied allegations that his party provided direct funding to the Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) protests. However, he openly justified the party's provision of logistical support to the agitating youth, framing the assistance as a moral imperative to support democratic dissent. This stance highlights a deepening divide between the Congress leadership and the ruling administration, as the party attempts to align itself with student-led movements while distancing itself from claims of financial orchestration. By positioning the government’s educational policies as a failure, Hariprasad is effectively leveraging current civil unrest to challenge the central authority’s governance record and mobilize support among the younger demographic.
why_it_matters_bullets: This development signals a strategic shift in opposition tactics, where political parties are increasingly formalizing their support for grassroots movements to challenge the central government's policy failures. The move risks escalating political polarization while simultaneously forcing a national conversation on educational reform and the limits of institutional support for civil protests.

sources.headline: Haveri University circular on compulsory attendance for Ayudha Puja draws protest
sources.content: A group of writers, academics, journalists and social activists has urged the Chief Minister and the Higher Education Minister to intervene

brief_bullets: Haveri University in Karnataka has ignited a significant controversy after issuing an official circular mandating the attendance of all students and staff at an Ayudha Puja ceremony held on campus. This directive prompted a swift and organized backlash from a coalition of prominent writers, academics, journalists, and social activists who argue that such compulsory religious observances violate the secular principles governing public educational institutions. The protesting group has formally petitioned the Chief Minister and the Higher Education Minister, demanding immediate intervention to rescind the order and ensure that university spaces remain neutral and inclusive for all students regardless of their personal beliefs. Critics contend that the university administration’s decision oversteps its academic mandate, potentially alienating students from diverse backgrounds and setting a concerning precedent for the integration of religious rituals into state-funded academic environments. The situation remains tense as stakeholders await a formal response from the state government regarding the preservation of secular academic standards.
why_it_matters_bullets: This incident highlights the escalating tension between traditional religious practices and secular governance within India's public education system, potentially setting a legal and social precedent for how state-funded universities manage religious neutrality. Failure to address these concerns risks deepening institutional polarization and undermining the constitutional mandate of secularism in academic spaces.

brief_bullets: Sri Lanka has been plunged into a total islandwide blackout, leaving millions of citizens and critical infrastructure without electricity as authorities scramble to identify the root cause of the collapse. While the exact trigger remains under investigation, government officials have pointed to a significant failure at a major hydropower station in the central hill country that was initially detected just one day prior to the widespread disruption. This cascading failure highlights the extreme fragility of the nation’s power grid, which has struggled to maintain stability amidst ongoing economic volatility and aging infrastructure. As energy engineers work to restore the national supply, the incident has reignited public concerns regarding the reliability of the state-run utility provider and the government's ability to manage essential services during a period of intense national recovery. The blackout serves as a stark reminder of the systemic vulnerabilities that continue to threaten Sri Lanka's path toward long-term economic and social stabilization.

brief_bullets: The Delhi government has formally proposed a strict cap of 2.5 lakh e-rickshaws operating within the national capital to address mounting concerns regarding traffic congestion and road safety. This regulatory initiative, spearheaded by the Transport Department, aims to streamline the chaotic proliferation of battery-operated vehicles that have become a primary mode of last-mile connectivity but currently lack systematic oversight. By establishing a definitive ceiling on the number of permits, authorities intend to curb the unregulated growth of these vehicles, which frequently contribute to gridlock and safety hazards on arterial roads. The proposal reflects a broader strategic shift toward formalizing the city's informal transit sector while balancing the necessity of sustainable, green mobility solutions. Officials are now evaluating the implementation framework, which will likely involve a transition toward digitized registration and stricter enforcement of designated operational zones to ensure urban mobility remains efficient and orderly.
why_it_matters_bullets: This policy marks a critical transition from unchecked expansion to managed urban planning, setting a precedent for how rapidly growing megacities can integrate sustainable transit without compromising infrastructure capacity or public safety.

sources.headline: Six years after jumping parole, life convict arrested in Chickballapur

brief_bullets: After evading authorities for six years, a convicted murderer serving a life sentence was finally apprehended by police in Chickballapur, Karnataka. The individual, who had been granted parole in 2018, failed to return to prison as mandated, effectively becoming a fugitive from justice. Local law enforcement officials successfully tracked the convict’s movements, leading to a coordinated operation that resulted in his arrest and subsequent return to custody. This capture marks the conclusion of a lengthy manhunt that had remained an open case for state correctional authorities. The incident highlights significant vulnerabilities in the parole monitoring system, raising questions regarding the oversight mechanisms used to track high-risk offenders once they are released into the community. The convict is now expected to face additional legal repercussions for his abscondence, further extending his time behind bars while prompting a review of existing surveillance protocols for parolees.
why_it_matters_bullets: The arrest underscores critical gaps in judicial oversight and parole enforcement, signaling a likely shift toward more rigorous monitoring and automated tracking systems for life-term convicts to prevent future security lapses.

stories.primary_headline: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked

primary_source.headline: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked
primary_source.content: Many of the records accessed were sensitive and held "intimate information" the panel said A West Midlands Police misconduct hearing acknowledged PC Shannon Parsons felt "isolated and disconnected" due to working part-time and returning from maternity leave, but had breached standards of professional behaviour. Parsons had claimed there was a policing purpose to her searches, the panel said, and was seeking to "keep herself up to date, informed and was often in a position to support and assist other colleagues in operational matters". However, chair of the panel Debra Tedds concluded the searches were carried out for the officer's "own personal benefit". As a result, Parsons was dismissed without notice and barred from future work in policing. The searches took part over a period of about five years, the panel heard, and many included incidents near her home address.

stories.primary_headline: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson

primary_source.headline: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
primary_source.content: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure ...I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you”, I’ve never clicked so fast. Knowledge is power, after all, and the promised signals came courtesy of psychologists via a magazine with the word science in its title.The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

primary_source.headline: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
primary_source.content: Watch: Polanski says practical application of Zionism is racist The Green leader told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, it would be party policy until 2028. The motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month, described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population". He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 - a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members - in Brighton earlier this month. The motion also asserted the party's backing for "a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine", a full arms embargo on Israel and a commitment to Palestinian liberation. Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

stories.primary_headline: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

primary_source.headline: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme
primary_source.content: Since 2018 the BBC has offered six-month secondment opportunities for up to two civil servant statisticians to work for BBC News's head of statistics. A BBC spokesperson said: "All BBC journalism and editorial decisions are made by BBC journalists and editors, in line with the BBC's editorial guidelines, so the statisticians never make editorial decisions." Those currently on secondment would not be involved in the publication of news or content during the review and the current round of recruitment will be paused while the role is reviewed, the corporation added. The decision follows a report in The Telegraph which said embedded civil servants  had been engaging in editorial tasks and raised questions about a breach of impartiality rules. The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards". They said although statisticians' work had sometimes been recognised with their names on the BBC website, "they never made editorial decisions".

stories.primary_headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray

primary_source.headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray
primary_source.content: Mumbai: A day after Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray backed the ‘regime change’ call, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday took a dig at him saying he could not prevent a regime change in his own party. Fadnavis was referring to the June-July 2022 rebellion in the Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde — who toppled Thackeray’s Maha Vikas Aghadi government with the help of BJP to become the Chief Minister. Slamming Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Thackeray on Saturday said: “Yes we are ready for a regime change…particularly If right to express ourselves through vote and right to protest is being taken away then we have to change regime.”Uddhav Thackeray backs Prashant Bhushan's regime change call, cites curbs on voting, protest rightsHowever, Fadnavis, on Sunday hit back at Thackeray, a former ally, who is now a key leader of the Congress-led INDIA opposition bloc. stories.primary_headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile

primary_source.headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
primary_source.content: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years agoA few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”.Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather

primary_source.headline: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
primary_source.content: Sirisha Bandla (right), pictured with expedition lead Steve Schultz, said the crew was "really excited" A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery. The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate. Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday. "We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku. The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.

stories.primary_headline: India's education system is an 'exclusion' plan keeping youth out, alleges Rahul Gandhi

primary_source.headline: India's education system is an 'exclusion' plan keeping youth out, alleges Rahul Gandhi
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday criticised the education system in India, calling it an "exclusion system" that is designed to keep millions of youth out.His remarks came during an interaction he had with students recently, a video of which was posted on his social media handles.Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers"If you don’t have money, power, or don't speak English, the system will push you out without a second thought. You can’t call this an education system. It’s an exclusion system - designed to keep millions of Indian youth out," he said.He said what the current system is doing is certifying people and creating a "fake idea of merit".&nbsp;His comments came as a student said the National Education Policy is exclusionary with most of the students not being able to pursue studies in regular colleges owing to the Common University Entrance Test.

stories.primary_headline: Show HN: The Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake

primary_source.headline: Show HN: The Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake
primary_source.content:
I made this ahead of the Ocarina of Time remake which comes out in 17 days. I remember the feeling of playing it as a kid but I hadn’t kept up with the story so I built a timeline to catch up before the Door of Time reopens.Nintendo’s own timeline is the authority here (Hyrule Historia and their chronicle page). The fun part was rethinking how to visualize it. It branches at the end of Ocarina into three eras depending on whether Link wins or loses, so each era is its own thread on the cloth. The threads meet again much later with Breath of the Wild.I had a lot of help from Claude. I’d often thought about building things like this but never found the time between the day job and the rest of life.

brief_bullets: Microsoft has officially withdrawn as the anchor tenant for a massive AI datacentre project in Loughton, Essex, citing significant concerns regarding the reliability and availability of local power supplies. Developed by the British firm Nscale, the facility was previously championed by UK government ministers as the nation’s largest AI-focused infrastructure project, intended to bolster domestic technological capacity by 2026. This sudden departure represents a major setback for the development, which relied heavily on Microsoft’s commitment to justify its scale and operational viability. The decision highlights the growing friction between the UK’s ambitious AI industrial strategy and the practical limitations of its aging national energy grid. As demand for high-density computing power surges, this project’s instability underscores the critical infrastructure bottlenecks that threaten to impede the country's aspirations to become a global leader in artificial intelligence. The project's collapse exposes a critical vulnerability in the UK's digital infrastructure strategy, where energy grid capacity is failing to keep pace with the massive power requirements of modern AI datacentres. This failure risks deterring future foreign investment and stalling the government's broader economic goals for the technology sector.

stories.primary_headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga

primary_source.headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga
primary_source.content: Some yogis welcome the idea of competition – for others, it is anathema. Will those keen for yoga to become an Olympic sport win the argument?Vaishnavi Saravanakumar describes herself on Instagram as “India’s rubber band girl”. In a typical video post, dressed in a rhinestone-studded crimson catsuit and accompanied by a Bollywood-rap anthem, she demonstrates an improbable feat. From standing, she snakes into a deep back bend, curls her head and shoulders up under her tiger-striped calves, and finishes beaming to camera with ankles crossed under her chin. This is yoga as we have seldom seen it before.Earlier this year, the Indian government announced that it will push for yogasana’s inclusion in the Olympics, ahead of the country’s bid to host the 2036 Games. The news came the week before the inaugural World Yogasana Championship, held in Ahmedabad in June, at which Saravanakumar, a gold medallist, was one of 522 yogis competing. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: BJP's Yediyurappa alleges CM Shivakumar part of plot to dethrone Siddaramaiah

primary_source.headline: BJP's Yediyurappa alleges CM Shivakumar part of plot to dethrone Siddaramaiah
primary_source.content: Davanagere: BJP Parliamentary Board member and former Chief Minister B S Yediyurappa charged that many leaders including Chief Minister D K Shivakumar hatched a conspiracy to dethrone Siddaramaiah from the post of chief minister.Addressing media persons, here on Sunday, he stated that tolerance of Siddaramaiah is difficult to understand, but noted that the truth will soon come to light. He remarked that a systematic plot was executed to remove Siddaramaiah from the top post and create chaos in the state. D K Shivakumar is intoxicated by power and shows no willingness to correct his mistakes.HDK, JD(S) workers stage protest outside DGP office, demand immediate arrest of Rakesh Shetty over 'sting op' videosResponding to a question, he said, the state government is oblivious to the drought situation and the hardships faced by the people and farmers. It is displaying the height of irresponsibility at every turn. Despite having a vast majority, the Congress is running a 'Tughlaq-style' (arbitrary and chaotic) administration. The people must teach them a fitting lesson in the next election.Meanwhile, Chitradurga MP Govind Karjol urged that those in politics should serve as role models for society rather than acting like 'demons.' He called for an end to such low-level politics and demanded strict legal action against those who engage in despicable acts like 'sting operations.'

primary_source.headline: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
primary_source.content: Parisians wake up to protest damage and looted shops Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful. They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools. Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings. Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas. President Emmanuel Macron was due to address the nation at 20:00 local time on Sunday after what has been described as one of the worst outbreaks of disorder in modern French history.

stories.primary_headline: Unacceptable, says Chirag on Imran Khan’s protest

primary_source.headline: Unacceptable, says Chirag on Imran Khan’s protest
primary_source.content: Patna: Union Minister Chirag Paswan has slammed actor Imran Khan for protesting in India against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and called Khan’s act as “an attempt to create anarchy, backed by foreign powers.”Paswan, who made his film debut in 2011 opposite Kangana Ranaut in the movie Miley Naa Miley Hum, said, “I like the work of Imran Khan. I rate him high as an actor. But foreign nationals like Imran Khan should not have protested in India. I am not against peaceful protests by Indians. But if a foreign national protests or holds demonstrations, then it’s absolutely unacceptable,” said Paswan, backing the Indian Government’s decision asking Imran, nephew of Aamir Khan, to leave India this month itself.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeThe LJP (R) president, who is also a Lok Sabha member from Bihar’s Hajipur was speaking to mediamen here on Sunday about actor Imran Khan who is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder. “Why should someone, who is not an Indian citizen, get involved in the internal affairs of our country. As part of the Indian Government, I am concerned over attempts being made to create anarchy in India with the support of foreign powers,” said Paswan, who himself made an unsuccessful bid in Bollywood before joining the hurly burly of Indian politics after his debut movie ‘Miley Naa Miley Hum’ sank like a ‘Titanic’ at the box-office.Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers Chirag also slammed Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for going ahead with his Goa rally. “See the difference. On the one hand, Union Home Minister Amit Shah cancelled his engagements in view of the Kolkata tragedy. On the other hand, we have Rahul Gandhi for whom only politics matters. This is the contrast,” said Chirag, while slamming the Congress leader.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers

primary_source.headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday participated in the party's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Margao, walking two kilometres alongside party workers and leaders.Gandhi arrived at Dabolim airport in the afternoon to join the mass outreach programme. He is scheduled to address a public gathering at the Margao Cricket Club (MCC) ground later in the day.Among those who accompanied him during the yatra were AICC Goa desk in-charge Manikrao Thakare, co-in-charge Dr Anjali Nimbalkar, Leader of Opposition Yuri Alemao and Goa Pradesh Congress Committee president Girish Chodankar.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Alemao and Chodankar, began on September 22 and concluded on Sunday. The campaign covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in Goa as the Congress seeks to strengthen its grassroots network ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'The party described the 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', which translates to a campaign to protect Goa, as a movement to safeguard the state's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity.Throughout the campaign, the Congress highlighted concerns over land conversion, alleged land grabbing, unemployment, corruption and public safety, while emphasising the need to preserve Goa's distinct social and cultural identity.The yatra also aimed to engage with local communities and bring development-related issues to the forefront of political discussions.With the 2027 Goa Assembly elections approaching, the Congress is seeking to expand its grassroots presence and mobilise support across constituencies, including those currently represented by the ruling BJP.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy

primary_source.headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy
primary_source.content: Critics mock it as raunchy trash – but this enchanting genre is much older, and wilder, than you might imagineThere’s a popular genre, filled with beautiful, human-sized fairies having sex with humans (often quite violent sex, but the people reading it seem to enjoy it). Word is that it’s badly written and unashamedly escapist – all golden, glittering palaces, wild adventure and, of course, gorgeous fairies. It’s certainly popular – plenty of the stories have been translated into numerous languages, spreading across continents. Serious commentators are sure it spells bad news: at best, it’s just a load of trash; at worst, it’s actively leading people astray. Most damningly of all, women produce and consume it. Welcome to the 12th century, where fairy romance is all the rage. Sound familiar?The romantasy that fills our shelves and bestseller lists – from Sarah J Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses to Callie Hart’s Quicksilver – is not a new genre, but part of a centuries-old heritage. You only need to look at the medieval predecessors of the modern romantasy novel to understand why it’s enjoyed by millions and why, even after hundreds of years, fairy romance has such power over us – and why there are still those who want to diminish and dismiss it. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas

primary_source.headline: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas
primary_source.content: The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreamsDepending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse. Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland. Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”. The president was endorsing him.Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks. He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music

primary_source.headline: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music
primary_source.content: Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowdsFor the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture

primary_source.headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture
primary_source.content: A new Washington DC exhibition examines how Toni Morrison, Maya Angelou and more used the Bard’s work to help tell their own stories“William Shakespeare was a black woman.” In 1985, Maya Angelou spoke these words as part of a keynote speech at a convention in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.There, she spoke of the role poetry played in her transition from muteness as a child and how she fantasized herself triumphantly delivering Portia’s speech from William Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice in front of her entire community at church. Though she never got the chance to perform that rendition, Angelou acknowledged her desire to deliver that rendition as part of a lifelong kinship with Shakespeare, a connection she continued to seek out throughout her life whenever she needed heartening or solace. In her eyes, Shakespeare wrote his emotionally desolate Sonnet 29 “for” her; how else could he have so aptly described the harsh realities of the Black feminine condition? Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: More peas, please! 17 delicious ways to devour Britain’s most brilliant vegetable

primary_source.headline: More peas, please! 17 delicious ways to devour Britain’s most brilliant vegetable
primary_source.content: They’re healthy, versatile, sustainable and available. Yet pea consumption in the UK is at a 50-year low. Here are the curries, dips, pasta dishes and even cakes that could turn all that aroundIt’s not good news for the pea farmers: pea consumption in the UK has fallen to a 50-year low. According to data from Defra, the average Briton ate just 37g of peas per week in 2025, down from 144g per week in 1975.Though a classic British staple, peas are not for everybody. Apparently only 22% of gen Z associate peas with Britain at all (which is patently ridiculous: 90% of the peas we consume in the UK are grown here, while we produce about 160,000 tonnes for freezing alone each year). stories.primary_headline: Guwahati Airport Launches 'Utsav Aarambh' For Durga Puja

primary_source.headline: Guwahati Airport Launches 'Utsav Aarambh' For Durga Puja
primary_source.content: The initiative marks the airport's first festive engagement at the arrival forecourt, bringing together Durga Puja-themed displays, traditional handicrafts, regional art, music and local food.

sources.headline: Guwahati Airport Launches 'Utsav Aarambh' For Durga Puja
sources.content: The initiative marks the airport's first festive engagement at the arrival forecourt, bringing together Durga Puja-themed displays, traditional handicrafts, regional art, music and local food.

brief_bullets: Guwahati’s Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport has officially inaugurated 'Utsav Aarambh,' a festive initiative designed to immerse arriving passengers in the cultural vibrancy of the Durga Puja season. This inaugural engagement transforms the airport’s arrival forecourt into a curated showcase of Assamese heritage, featuring intricate traditional handicrafts, regional artistic displays, and live musical performances. By integrating local culinary offerings and thematic decorations, the airport authority aims to elevate the passenger experience while celebrating the region's deep-rooted cultural identity during India's most significant festive period. This strategic move marks the first time the facility has utilized its transit space for such an extensive cultural activation, effectively positioning the airport as a gateway that reflects the spirit and traditions of Northeast India to both domestic and international travelers. This initiative shifts the airport from a purely functional transit hub to a cultural touchpoint, strengthening regional branding and enhancing passenger satisfaction through experiential engagement. It sets a new precedent for how infrastructure projects can leverage local heritage to foster community connection and boost regional tourism appeal.

It sets a new precedent for how infrastructure projects can leverage local heritage to foster community connection and boost regional tourism appeal.

This strategic move marks the first time the facility has utilized its transit space for such an extensive cultural activation, effectively positioning the airport as a gateway that reflects the spirit and traditions of Northeast India to both domestic and international travelers. This initiative shifts the airport from a purely functional transit hub to a cultural touchpoint, strengthening regional branding and enhancing passenger satisfaction through experiential engagement. It sets a new precedent for how infrastructure projects can leverage local heritage to foster community connection and boost regional tourism appeal.

stories.primary_headline: James Cameron congratulates Marvel as Avengers: Endgame surpasses Avatar at box office

primary_source.headline: James Cameron congratulates Marvel as Avengers: Endgame surpasses Avatar at box office

sources.headline: James Cameron congratulates Marvel as Avengers: Endgame surpasses Avatar at box office

brief_bullets: In a gesture of industry camaraderie, legendary filmmaker James Cameron publicly congratulated Marvel Studios and the team behind Avengers: Endgame after the superhero epic officially surpassed his 2009 blockbuster Avatar to become the highest-grossing film in cinematic history. Cameron shared a stylized image of an Iron Man-inspired Na'vi on social media, acknowledging the monumental achievement of the Marvel Cinematic Universe in capturing the global zeitgeist. This milestone marked the culmination of a decade-long narrative arc for the franchise, signaling a significant shift in the commercial dominance of serialized superhero storytelling. While Avatar had held the top spot for nearly ten years, the success of Endgame underscored the unprecedented power of fan engagement and the strategic expansion of the Disney-owned Marvel brand. This exchange between two of the industry's most influential creative forces highlights the mutual respect shared among filmmakers who operate at the pinnacle of global box office performance. This transition of the all-time box office crown validates the long-term viability of interconnected cinematic universes and reinforces Disney's unparalleled dominance in the modern theatrical landscape.

primary_source.headline: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool | Sid Lowe
primary_source.content: It will be a tense time for Europe’s longest serving president, despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much.But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey

primary_source.headline: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey
primary_source.content: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season bluesA Kalkan sunset is always a beautiful thing – the horseshoe-shaped bay deepening to azure blue against an apricot-rose sky – but, in October, when the light is low and the sun drops early, it’s almost transcendentally lovely. In some Turkish resorts, you’d be sitting watching it surrounded by quiet streets, half-empty bars and that melancholic sense that another season is over. In Kalkan, it still feels like summer; the harbourfront restaurants throng with visitors, the day gulets (wooden boats) still putter in and out of the bay and you don’t have to wait an hour to get a taxi back to your villa.
